e: Wasting 2 days reinventing responsive UI in Godot, squashing localization bugs, and finding a hidden 100-view YouTube goldmine for smart NPC AI.
s:
my biggest mistake so far wasting 2 days reinventing responsive ui in godot, squashing localization bugs, and finding a hidden 100-view youtube goldmine for smart npc ai. game development godot daily note  
i have made the biggest mistake. i thought that godot didn't have a responsive ui, so i spent 2 days building a custom class to manage ui dynamically only to learn later that godot actually does have built-in ways to make responsive uis.

but everything is not doom and gloom! i installed dialog manager, which is a very beautiful piece of software. i also fixed some bugs with my localization approach (it wasn't very fun, man i hate bug fixes).

and somehow, while scrolling youtube, i got recommended a video that had only 100 views. i clicked it and found an absolute gold mine. i will talk about it more later, but for now, it's a plugin for implementing ai not that kind of ai, ai for npcs and monsters. it's called goap, and here is the plugin.

t: The two elephant in the room
e: Tody i have deal with the tow elephant in the room
s:
the two elephant in the room tody i have deal with the tow elephant in the room game development godot problems & solutions programming  
today i did a hell of a lot of work! i added multiplayer and translation to my game, and it makes me feel very happy right now.
🌐 localhost multiplayer (for everyone)
## easy part : multiplayer (local host)
let's talk about how i did it. i added localhost multiplayer so anyone can port-forward and play with friends online, or play locally right in their house.

nowadays, developers don't add this because they rely strictly on steam multiplayer. i'll add steam support too, but i want people who can't afford my game to have the exact same experience.

i'm someone who had no credit card, so every game i played growing up was pirated. that's why i want everyone to have the freedom to play and enjoy my game if thy can not pay.

## the hard part: custom translation system

godot has enet, so multiplayer was relatively smooth, plus i know some cybersecurity stuff. but the translation part? that was the real challenge.

    the problem is godot's built-in localization loads every single language into memory all at once.

so my solution was i modified the default system to load only 2 languages:

        english (default fallback)

        the player's selected language

if a specific translation is missing, the game doesn't crash it seamlessly falls back to english.

also i even built a custom plugin to convert .csv files into .translation files.



man i'm kind of tired after all this architecture work. i think i'm going to watch some dragon ball now!

t: How I Stopped Quitting and Started Mking Game
e: Things I Did Before Creating My Game And You Should To...
s:
how i stopped quitting and started mking game things i did before creating my game and you should to... game development godot programming problems & solutions  
all my life, i haven't finished a single game. i always start, make a mess, and then quit. so this time, i have done something different i planned for a few days, not for eternity (some people plan for eternity). here is what i decided:

i will start with my software architecture, and my choices are dependency injection, context-based hierarchy system, and 'signals up, call down.' these are the core things in my software architecture.

in code, i decided that every piece of code has to be inside a function. if i am doing something big, i will divide it into smaller functions because i think commenting is bad, code shouldn't need comments. only after creating clean code do i use comments.

and i decided that i will add multiplayer and translation before i create the game, which will save a lot of time in the long run.

that's most of it about what i did before creating the game. also, i created this website to keep a record of my journey.
